developers.name: Inmobilia
developers.summary: A Mérida-based developer of large planned communities whose Tulum presence centres on Tulum 101, a master-planned district of residential, hospitality and mixed-use projects.
description: Inmobilia is a real estate developer headquartered in Mérida, Yucatán, with more than three decades of activity across southern Mexico. Its portfolio spans golf communities, tourism, luxury housing, mixed-use districts and corporate space, including Yucatan Country Club and Vía Montejo in Mérida and Four Seasons Caye Chapel in Belize. The company reports more than 7.8 million square metres developed and often works through partnerships with hotel operators, architecture studios and other developers.

In Tulum, its main undertaking is Tulum 101, which the company presents as the first master-planned community of macro-lots in the destination. The plan divides land into parcels for housing, hotels and commerce, with other developers building individual projects inside it, such as SIMCA's Gran Tulum. Inmobilia also markets branded residential projects in Tulum, among them Mayaliah Tulum MGallery and Faena Residences Tulum, reflecting a focus on hospitality-linked homes.

projects.name: Tulum 101
projects.description: A gated master plan near the beach divided into macro-lots for residential, hotel and commercial use, with underground utilities and fibre optics. It hosts several sub-projects by Inmobilia and partner developers.

projects.name: Nido by Tulum 101
projects.description: A private enclave of 85 single-family lots within Tulum 101, organised around wide roads, open space and a clubhouse under the 'Jungle Nesting' concept.

projects.name: Ramia by Tulum 101
projects.description: A community of 71 lots of roughly 280 to 375 m² set into the natural landscape of the Tulum 101 master plan.

projects.name: 101 Park
projects.description: A 55-unit residential community inside Tulum 101 with rooftop pools and a series of themed outdoor parks.

projects.name: Humana Tulum
projects.description: A mixed-use project split between 63 residences and 45 hotel keys, each with its own amenities plus shared spaces.

projects.name: Mayaliah Tulum MGallery
projects.description: A jungle-set project combining 95 branded private residences with a 45-room boutique hotel under the MGallery label, with a concept drawn from Maya traditions.

projects.name: Faena Residences Tulum
projects.description: A Faena-branded community of 147 homes designed by architect Brandon Haw, using wood and chukum finishes with rooftop gardens and pools, presented on Inmobilia's site.

developers.name: SIMCA
developers.summary: A southeast-Mexico developer with residential, industrial and retail divisions, active in Tulum through condominium projects in Aldea Zamá, La Veleta and the Tulum 101 master plan.
description: SIMCA (legal name Real Estate SIMCA SAPI de CV) is a Mexican developer working across the Yucatán Peninsula and Tabasco, with sales offices in Mérida, Playa del Carmen and Tulum. Beyond housing, it runs divisions for industrial and logistics parks, retail and business space. Its residential catalogue ranges from large lot subdivisions and golf communities around Mérida to apartment buildings near the beach in Playa del Carmen.

In Tulum, SIMCA concentrates on mid-size condominium buildings in established residential zones. Costa Caribe sits in Aldea Zamá, between the town and the beach; Gran Tulum is located inside Inmobilia's Tulum 101 master plan; and Natal is in La Veleta. Earlier Tulum projects include Querido Tulum, designed with the studio Reyes Ríos + Larraín and nominated for ArchDaily's Building of the Year, and Prana. The company also operates a vacation-rental and property-management program for owners.

developers.name: TAO México
developers.summary: A residential developer focused on resort destinations, with jungle communities in Tulum and further projects in Akumal, Puerto Aventuras and Puerto Vallarta.
description: TAO México develops residential communities in Mexican resort destinations, chiefly the Riviera Maya, with additional activity in Puerto Vallarta and Los Cabos. The company reports more than 19 years in the market and over 23 residential communities, and it is associated with a charitable foundation, Fundación TAO. Many of its earlier developments are clustered around Akumal, within the Tulum Country Club residential complex.

Its Tulum work centres on low-rise communities set in the jungle, a few minutes by road from the town centre and the beach.TAO Tulum, in Aldea Zamá, combines apartments and penthouses with pools, a gym and a yoga deck, while Edena Tulum is a six-hectare private community of houses and flats with walking paths and shared amenities. Nearby, the company has built Sek and Naraina in Akumal and TAO Náutico on the canals of Puerto Aventuras, extending a design approach that emphasises privacy, landscaping and wellness facilities.

developers.name: Grupo R4 Yucatán
developers.summary: A Yucatán Peninsula developer with residential projects in Yucatán and Quintana Roo, including three condominium buildings in Tulum's Aldea Zamá area.
description: Grupo R4 Yucatán is a real estate group operating in Yucatán and Quintana Roo, with work in Mérida and the Yucatán coast as well as Playa del Carmen and Tulum. Alongside development, it lists services such as architectural design, urbanisation and landscaping, construction and turnkey projects, and it works with a network of local and international brokers. The group cites more than 35 years of experience and over 35 projects.

Its Tulum portfolio is concentrated in Aldea Zamá, within the Selvazama master plan between the town and the beach. Carey Tulum Condos draws on a reinterpretation of pre-Hispanic Maya building methods; Cautiva is a 71-apartment building with a commercial area; and Déjà Vu comprises two towers with 45 residences and a wellness-oriented amenity programme. In Playa del Carmen the group has Altra Beach Condos and Olaya, while its Yucatán projects include Puerto Lindo in Chelem and Viacholul near Mérida.
